approach: A culture lesson for adults: what greeting with a kiss, a handshake or an abrazo looks like in different countries, how to respond without awkwardness, and the words said while doing it.
coverage: In most of Latin America friends and acquaintances greet with one light cheek kiss
The cheek kiss is usual between women and between a man and a woman
Men usually shake hands or give an abrazo; in Argentina and Uruguay male friends often kiss on the cheek too
In Spain the greeting is two kisses, one on each cheek
A first business meeting usually starts with a handshake; follow the other person's lead
An abrazo is a hug, often with a pat on the back; un abrazo also closes a message
In a small group, greet and say goodbye to each person
What to say: Hola, ¿cómo estás?, Mucho gusto, Encantado / Encantada

blocks.purpose: Explains what the cheek kiss is and who uses it, so the custom feels ordinary.

paragraphs: In most of Latin America, people who meet socially greet with one light kiss on the cheek. It is really a cheek-to-cheek touch with a small kiss sound, not a kiss with the lips on the skin.

It is usual between two women and between a man and a woman, among friends and family and often at a first introduction in a social setting. Men usually greet each other with a handshake or an abrazo.
In Argentina and Uruguay, male friends and relatives often greet each other with a cheek kiss as well. In Spain the greeting is two kisses, one on each cheek.

sections.heading: At work
paragraphs: A first business meeting usually starts with a handshake. Once people know each other, a cheek kiss at work is common in many countries. When in doubt, let the other person lead and match what they do.

data.question: At a dinner in Colombia, a woman you are meeting leans in for a cheek kiss. What is the most comfortable response?
choices: Lean in, touch cheeks lightly and say "Mucho gusto".
Step back and offer your hand instead.
Give a full hug and a kiss on each cheek.

trapReasons.1: At home a handshake feels like the safe, respectful choice.

data.whyIntuitionFailed: Visitors fear that the kiss is too personal, so they pull back. To the other person, pulling back can feel cold.
data.correctReasoning: She has signaled the greeting she expects. Match it: a light cheek touch with a kiss sound, and a phrase like Mucho gusto.
data.recoveryTip: Let the other person lead, then match what they do.

blocks.purpose: Closes with the one rule that covers every case.

data.takeaway: One cheek kiss in most of Latin America, two in Spain, a handshake to open a first business meeting, an abrazo among friends: and when unsure, follow the other person's lead.
